title: notes, and does not fail, a change no more than the noise
why: A change exactly as large as the noise would be read as a change: the comparison would call the noise a difference.

title: is fewer than 1% of the pixels more than 8 from the corner pixel
why: The blank frame's boundary moved: a frame holding exactly 1% of drawn pixels would be called blank.

title: counts a difference at the tolerance of 8, never below it
why: Differences judged at no tolerance: rasteriser noise of a few levels would read as a changed picture.

title: says two sizes differ in every pixel
why: Two shots of different sizes would reach the pixel comparison and throw, instead of being reported as a difference.

title: wants an export with nothing-drawn frames failed
why: An export whose first and last frames are the same, a motionless reel, would pass.

title: wants a new colour to rise from none
why: A line colour that is no more on the map than before it was chosen would pass.

title: fails under a threshold once one is set
why: A threshold set by a measuring run would fail the large changes and pass the small ones.

title: wants the face loaded, and only notes
why: A typeface that was chosen but did not change a label's measured width would pass.

title: asks the control as if the settings had changed
why: The manifest would hold no control pair, and the reviewer could not tell whether a reading is to be trusted.

title: keeps a shot as <id>.png, and throws for one that was not written
why: A shot that was never written would be kept as evidence without a word.

title: settles on the first two shots that agree
why: A picture that has stopped changing would never be known to have, and every shot would be reported as unsettled.

find: outcome: 'fail', said: 'no pixel changed in a second of playing'
replace: outcome: 'note', said: 'no pixel changed in a second of playing'
title: fails when the trains did not move in a second
why: A map whose trains do not move would be noted, not failed.

find: return { ...base, outcome: 'note', said: `${measured}; no threshold is set yet${unsteady}` }
replace: return { ...base, outcome: 'fail', said: `${measured}; no threshold is set yet${unsteady}` }
title: only notes the number while no threshold is set
why: A number with no threshold behind it would fail a step on the first run, before any measuring run set one.

title: only notes that nothing changed when the map was not steady
why: A map that was still moving would fail a step for showing no change.

title: records only a failed check as a problem
why: A note would fail a step on a first run, before any threshold has been measured.

title: leaves a step that is part not automated so
why: A step with a picture kept would read as a plain pass, and its not-automated part would be lost from the record.

title: fails a picture with nothing in it, only notes one nearly empty
why: A frame under the unmeasured 1% would fail a step.

title: does not judge a frame inside the opening
why: A GIF's title card, bare by design, would be judged for being empty.

title: wants the face loaded, and only notes
why: A label that measured the same, where the selector may have found nothing real, would fail a step.

title: asks the control as if the settings had changed
why: The manifest would say which entries are control pairs, and the reviewer's reading would not be blind.

title: orders the manifest by step and id
why: A control written straight after the entry it shadows would be recognised by its position.

title: only notes that nothing changed for a setting the picture need not show
why: A line order that moves no pixel of the map would fail the step, as it did on one system.

title: names the kept pictures at random
why: Kept names would be the same in every run, and the reviewer could work out which picture is which.

title: keeps no picture twice
why: A control built of copies of the pair's own shots would be picked out by comparing file hashes.

title: keeps a picture named by two entries once
why: A picture listed by two entries would be copied twice, and the copies would be byte for byte the same.

title: asks the control as if the settings had changed
why: The manifest would carry the machine checks, and a control's empty check would give it away.
